NH

sloppy and poor service outweighs the food
May 2026 • Family
Worst dining experience I’ve had in Vietnam due to sloppy service and miscommunications.

My friend and I came in around 7:30pm on a Friday. The restaurant was packed but there were still tables open. The front doors were closed, so I recommend going inside and sitting at an open table or finding a staff member.

My friend planned to order the canh chua cá hú/sour fish soup. The waitress asked what size, so my friend said small. The waitress then told her they only offer a large size that serves two, which confused us both because she was the one who asked us what size in the first place.

I ordered the Cơm tấm thịt heo nướng kiểu Thái/Thai-style grilled pork broken rice (95,000VND) and a nước dừa/fresh coconut juice (55,000VND). My friend got the Cá hú kho/braised fatty fish (89,000VND). Since the dish didn’t come with rice, she ordered a side of rice (20,000VND). The waitress confirmed in Vietnamese “hai đĩa cơm” (“two rice portions”). In retrospect I understand the logic, but it would’ve been clearer to just confirm one extra bowl of rice on the side since my dish already came with rice.

My friend and I both speak Vietnamese in a dialect that is different than the common Saigon dialect. She later ordered a fresh coconut juice in Vietnamese, pointed at the coconut, and even ordered in English for good measure. The waitress said OK, then came back asking if she wanted fresh coconut juice versus some other type. We were confused again since there was only one kind we’d pointed to on the table and we didn’t see another option on the menu. She came back again later to tell us they’d run out.

My food was good but the portion was on the smaller side. My friend’s fish was very fatty. I know this dish runs fatty, but the ratio of fish to fat was closer to 1:1.

The staff seemed indifferent and the service was poor and sloppy. Most staff were clustered at the back of the restaurant, blocking what I assumed was the bathroom. I genuinely couldn’t tell if one existed from where I sat (not far). One staff member stood near the door but faced inward toward the restaurant, which made it uncomfortable if you were facing them.

No water was brought to the table and no wet wipes or napkins were offered. Dishes like cơm tấm with pork chop can be eaten by hand and even smaller street stalls typically offer wipes as a baseline. When the bathroom is hard to access and nothing is at the table, it feels inconsiderate. For a restaurant with this many reviews and a nicer setup than most places in the area, the service was a real letdown.

They do accept card, which was a plus. Our total came out to 279,720VND/$10.60 (259,000VND for the meal plus an 8% tax of 20,720VND).

I try to be fair with reviews, but this is one instance where the general consensus was accurate. The couple sitting next to us had a similar experience - I overheard them commenting about being brought the wrong amount of what they’d ordered. The food just isn’t good enough to make up for the experience.
